learn.canDo: Turn incidents into error-budget minutes for a chosen SLO, and set burn-rate alerts that catch floods and leaks without paging on blips.
learn.why: SLOs and error budgets are how reliability is traded against change. Burn-rate alerting is the usual follow-up.
learn.keyIdea: Page on how fast the budget burns.

learn.canDo: Choose metrics, traces and logs to detect, locate and explain an incident within a budget, using tail sampling and correlation ids.
learn.why: Observability spend is easy to overdo or underdo. Tying each signal to a question shows judgement.
learn.keyIdea: Metrics detect, traces locate, logs explain.

learn.canDo: Compare all-at-once, rolling, blue-green and canary releases by users exposed and time to roll back, and size a canary.
learn.why: Safe deploys are a standard senior topic. The canary-sizing detail separates memorised from understood answers.
learn.keyIdea: Limit the audience and shorten the way back.

learn.canDo: Plan a flag rollout with a small first step and a fast kill switch, and stop flag debt with owners and expiry dates.
learn.why: Flags decouple deploy from release. Their costs, dead branches and slow switches, are the follow-up.
learn.keyIdea: A flag is a loan; somebody must pay it back.

learn.canDo: Classify dependencies as critical or optional, add fallbacks, and shed optional work under overload.
learn.why: Availability multiplies down with every required dependency. Degrading gracefully is how pages survive bad days.
learn.keyIdea: Not everything on a page is the page.

learn.canDo: Meet stated RPO and RTO targets with backups, replicas or cross-region copies, and prove them with restore drills.
learn.why: Recovery targets drive disaster recovery cost. Knowing that replication is not a backup is a classic check.
learn.keyIdea: A backup nobody has restored is a hope.

learn.canDo: Compare single region, active-passive and active-active on downtime, latency, data loss and cost.
learn.why: Going multi-region is a large commitment. Pricing it against the real failure rate is the senior answer.
learn.keyIdea: Fix outages with a standby, distance with active-active.

learn.canDo: Combine detection, automatic failover, DNS, replication and degradation into a region-loss plan within a budget.
learn.why: A region failure tests every operations choice at once. The skill is finding the slowest link.
learn.keyIdea: Add up the minutes, then attack the longest.

chapter.story: Pigeon becomes a service people depend on, and the team learns to run it: measure it, ship it carefully, and survive its worst day.
outcomes: Set SLOs and alerts that mean something
Release changes with a small blast radius
Plan recovery and multi-region with numbers
chapter.why: Running a system is a different skill from building it. Each practice here converts a vague worry into a number you can act on.
chapter.payoff: In an interview you can describe how you would measure, release and recover a service. At work you will recognise which of these your team is missing.
